quotes.text: The result is a new underwriting rule. Validation proves demand; it does not prove independence.
A platform serving an overlapping user base can bundle adjacent functionality, share identity and data, and price the new feature below the level at which a standalone company can survive
Data may remain, but only if the company has lawful rights to reuse them, connects them to outcomes, and can carry the learning across customers.
The durable layer is the project, policy, identity, and history that remain when the provider changes.
The business brand should not be identical to AssistOS or any current component.

A small room with ten people, a clear purpose, a persistent AI facilitator, shared memory, status rituals, and consequences can create more social value than a technically impressive but institutionally empty city.
A fork is not a meaningful right if contributors lose all reputation and economic history when they leave.
The principle is shared research, separate companies, convergent brands.
In return, validated learning from the venture should strengthen the common architecture where rights and confidentiality allow.
Shared infrastructure is valuable only when the same component genuinely solves a recurrent problem.
A negative result can be valuable if it prevents the studio from financing a false path.
The financing milestone should purchase a specific reduction in uncertainty or a specific increase in the asset stock.
Previous versions of a thesis should remain available, together with the reasons they changed.
Some ventures will remain independent specialists. Some will merge. Some will contribute technology to another company. Some will fail and leave behind useful knowledge.
